concern_results.conclusion: In the diff, the Makefile declares `export RUBYOPT` separately from the target-specific `override RUBYOPT :=` line. `announces_steps` checks each sentence or semicolon clause separately, so an optional offer elsewhere on the line no longer hides an unconditional step. The step check only fires with edit or delivery evidence. The liveness helper re-checks with signal 0 when procfs is missing. The high-impact probe now requires `blocked:` and forbids `continuing:`. All of this matches the acceptance list.

The hook only returns a recheck reason and grants no authority. Guidance on routine tests keeps explicit user limits, production, destructive, permission and new-purchase boundaries. Explicit stricter sign-off rules still bind and have their own probe. Eval runs use synthetic prompts with hooks disabled. I found no write path or unsafe mutation.

The `--replicas` argument is validated (exit 2), and replica errors stay ERROR. Without procfs, a live PID is not reported as exited. Missing `git ls-files` output and an empty Makefile scan both fail closed. Leg 3 stands down only when a host probe shows Ruby already reads UTF-8 under the C locale. Replica concurrency has no cap, but the caller chooses the count, so this is advisory, not blocking.

Each new behavior has negative controls: the Make mutations (no override, no export) must fail at runtime, the high-impact checks include contradictory and marker-only outputs, the optional-clause Stop cases must recheck, and the liveness checks mock a missing PID and a Linux zombie. These tests would fail if the risky behavior came back. The red/green runs themselves are the author's claims; I could not run them.

Existing CLI flags and exit codes are unchanged. `--replicas` is new and optional, and with one replica the result rows keep their old shape (no replica key). JSON output gains the additive `model_source`, `replicas` and `probes` keys. A caller `RUBYOPT` that sets a conflicting encoding is a documented residual.
Nothing needs migrating; the hook, prose and scripts can be reverted together. The package version bump to 0.18.7 comes from an earlier commit, and this update does not publish anything.
The runners print a notice when the default model is used, report pass counts for any probe that is not N of N, and print a marker when leg 3 cannot be evaluated.
The register rows and plans call the model samples advisory and make no general compliance claim. The plan's status stays interim until full validation finishes, which fits the pending full lane.

Sign-off is now scoped to merge or launch of high-impact paths, and explicit stricter rules still bind. Dev/test environment names do not authorize destructive or production actions, and paired probes enforce this.

Hook and script changes include deterministic tests, and the contracts' independent review/challenge requirement is acknowledged as pending before landing. The allowlist became stricter, not broader, and the plan records why. I found no contract violation.
